aspects.says: A rule's amount range is compared as a number of minor units and includes both of its ends.
basis: section:16.1 A Simulator's Rules Are Data, and the First Rule That Matches Decides

aspects.says: DelayFilter on the outgoing direction makes every answer slow and sleeps in the sending thread; a drop is a disconnect of the session's channel.
basis: section:16.2 A Listener Runs on the Session's Thread, So a Late Answer Is Scheduled
aspects.reason: Channel configuration and socket behaviour that only show with timing on a real connection; the graded runner keeps practices deterministic.

aspects.says: A simulator's behaviour is an ordered table: the first rule that applies answers, so exceptions go above ranges and the catch-all goes last.
basis: section:16.1 A Simulator's Rules Are Data, and the First Rule That Matches Decides

aspects.says: A scripted case grades every expected field and reports every difference in field order, with card numbers protected and a missing answer as a single failure.
basis: section:16.5 A Scripted Case Grades Every Field and Reports Every Failure

aspects.says: A proxy answers locally only for a request that never left; when the upstream host doesn't answer in time it sends nothing, and it relays the host's answer unchanged.
basis: section:16.4 A Proxy May Answer Only for a Request That Never Left
section:16.4.1 Spot the Problem: The Proxy That Helped

aspects.says: The proxy's record is the log event holding the messages, masked by the logger, while the messages it forwards stay clear.
basis: section:16.4.1 Spot the Problem: The Proxy That Helped

aspects.says: All of a proxy's clients share its one QMUX, so two clients with the same terminal ID and STAN collide as a duplicate key.
basis: section:16.4.2 One QMUX Serves Every Client of the Proxy

aspects.says: A proxy's upstream wait must be at least as long as its clients' wait, or it loses answers the client could still use.
basis: section:16.4.1 Spot the Problem: The Proxy That Helped

aspects.says: ISOServer calls listeners on the session's thread, so a listener that waits delays every later request on that connection; a late answer is handed off and process returns.
basis: section:16.2 A Listener Runs on the Session's Thread, So a Late Answer Is Scheduled

aspects.says: The simulator is deployed as a QServer request listener, one repeated rule property per row, with the real host's channel class and packager.
basis: section:16.1 A Simulator's Rules Are Data, and the First Rule That Matches Decides
aspects.reason: Deploy configuration; a graded run can't observe it, and the rule reading it feeds is graded in sheet-host.

aspects.says: A client can report the right outcome and still do the wrong thing, so a test asserts on what the simulator received, taken with a timeout from records that expire.
basis: section:16.3 The Simulator Is a Witness: Ask It What the Client Sent

aspects.says: A rule the simulator cannot read stops the configuration instead of being skipped, so a typo fails the deploy rather than quietly changing the answers.
basis: section:16.1 A Simulator's Rules Are Data, and the First Rule That Matches Decides
